extracted.intended_audience: employers petitioning for H-2B workers, their agents/attorneys, and USCIS/DOL adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and evidentiary standards for filing, processing, and enforcing H-2B (temporary nonagricultural) petitions, including special supplemental-cap allocations for FY2024 and FY2025, Guam-specific procedures, petition documentation, and employer obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must notify DHS, within 2 workdays, and beginning on a date and in a manner specified in a notice published in the Federal Register if: An H-2B worker does not report for work within 5 workdays after the employment start date stated on the petition; the nonagricultural labor or services for which H-2B workers were hired were completed more than 30 days early; or an H-2B worker does not report for work for a period of 5 consecutive workdays without the consent of the employer or is terminated prior to the completion of the nonagricultural labor or services for which they were hired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner must retain evidence of such notification and make it available for inspection by DHS officers for a 1-year period beginning on the date of the notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to government access and cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: In filing an H-2B petition, the petitioner and each employer (if different from the petitioner) consent to allow Government access to all sites where the labor is being or will be performed and agrees to fully cooperate with any compliance review, evaluation, verification, or inspection conducted by USCIS, including on-site inspection, review of employer records, and interview of employees and other individuals possessing pertinent information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews may be conducted in absence of employer or representatives and may occur on employer property or at a neutral location. Failure or refusal to cooperate may result in denial or revocation of any H-2B petition for workers performing services at inspected locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of temporary services or labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary services or labor under the H-2B classification refers to any job in which the petitioner's need for the duties to be performed by the employee(s) is temporary, whether or not the underlying job can be described as permanent or temporary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of petitioner's need — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment is of a temporary nature when the employer needs a worker for a limited period of time. The employer must establish that the need for the employee will end in the near, definable future. Generally, that period of time will be limited to one year or less, but in the case of a one-time event could last up to 3 years. The petitioner's need for the services or labor shall be a one-time occurrence, a seasonal need, a peak load need, or an intermittent need.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time occurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must establish that it has not employed workers to perform the services or labor in the past and that it will not need workers to perform the services or labor in the future, or that it has an employment situation that is otherwise permanent, but a temporary event of short duration has created the need for a temporary worker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonal need
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must establish that the services or labor is traditionally tied to a season of the year by an event or pattern and is of a recurring nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner shall specify the period(s) of time during each year in which it does not need the services or labor. The employment is not seasonal if the period during which the services or labor is not needed is unpredictable, subject to change, or is considered a vacation period for the petitioner's permanent employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peakload need
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must establish that it regularly employs permanent workers at the place of employment and needs to supplement permanent staff on a temporary basis due to a seasonal or short-term demand, and that the temporary additions will not become part of the petitioner's regular operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermittent need
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must establish that it has not employed permanent or full-time workers to perform the services or labor, but occasionally or intermittently needs temporary workers to perform services or labor for short periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-filing procedures and labor certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing a petition with the director to classify an alien as an H-2B worker, the petitioner shall apply for a temporary labor certification with the Secretary of Labor for all areas of the United States, except Guam (where application is to the Governor). The labor certification is advice to the director on whether U.S. workers capable of performing the services are available and whether the alien's employment will adversely affect wages and working conditions of similarly employed U.S. workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An H-2B petitioner shall be a U.S. employer, a U.S. agent, or a foreign employer filing through a U.S. agent. A foreign employer may not directly petition for H-2B but must use a U.S. agent authorized to file and accept service. The petitioner must consider available U.S. workers and offer terms consistent with the occupation and industry. A petitioner may not file unless a labor certification has been applied for within the prescribed time limits and a favorable determination obtained as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor certifications (except Guam): required findings and validity
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2B petition (except for Guam) shall be accompanied by an approved temporary labor certification from the Secretary of Labor stating that qualified U.S. workers are not available and that the alien's employment will not adversely affect wages and working conditions of similarly employed U.S. workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary of Labor may issue a temporary labor certification for up to one year. Temporary labor certifications for the U.S. Virgin Islands may be approved only for entertainers and athletes and only for periods not to exceed 45 days. Beginning with FY2010 petitions, the petition must state an employment start date that is the same as the date of need on the approved temporary labor certification; amended petitions due to unavailability may state a later start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor of Guam labor certification criteria and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2B petition for temporary employment on Guam shall be accompanied by an approved temporary labor certification issued by the Governor of Guam stating that qualified workers in the United States are not available and that the alien's employment will not adversely affect wages and working conditions of U.S. resident workers on Guam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Governor, in consultation with the Service, shall establish systematic methods for determining prevailing wage rates and availability of qualified U.S. residents. The prevailing wage system must consider wages/conditions in private and public sectors in Guam and/or the U.S., and advisory opinions (if used) must come from officially sanctioned groups reflecting a balance of interests. Availability rules include: advertise the position a minimum of three consecutive days in the newspaper with the largest daily circulation on Guam; place a job offer with the territorial job referral agency at least 30 days before need (may be reduced to 10 days for U.S. armed forces and entertainment industry); recruit in other U.S. areas if needed; report names of all U.S. applicants and hiring reasons; offer special considerations (housing/transport) to U.S. applicants; meet prevailing wage rates and working conditions determined; and agree to meet federal and territorial employment requirements such as nondiscrimination and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval, publication, reporting, and invalidation for Guam systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner must approve the systems to determine prevailing wages/working conditions and availability of U.S. resident workers (and modifications) prior to implementation; approved systems are published in the Federal Register and as public record in Guam. The Commissioner must approve construction wage data prior to implementation and surveys must be conducted at least every two years unless prescribed otherwise. The Governor must provide quarterly statistical data to the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Governor-issued temporary labor certification may be invalidated by a director if determined to involve fraud, willful misrepresentation, or gross error. If the director intends to invalidate, a notice of intent must be served detailing reasons and the employer has 30 days to file a written rebuttal; appeal of invalidation is available under part 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required with H-2B petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2B petition shall be accompanied by: (A) an approved temporary labor certification; (C) documentation that the alien qualifies for the job if the certification application requires certain education, training, experience, or special requirements; (D) a statement describing in detail the temporary situation or conditions necessitating the alien and stating whether the need is one-time, seasonal, peakload, or intermittent and whether recurrent; (E) liability for transportation costs — employer liable for reasonable costs of return transportation abroad if the alien is dismissed before end of authorized admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The liability provision applies even if the beneficiary voluntarily terminates employment (then not dismissed). If the beneficiary believes employer failed to comply, they shall advise the Service Center in writing; the complaint will be retained in the petition file. 'Abroad' means the alien's last place of foreign residence. Reserved subparagraphs are noted where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission period and authorized travel/extension windows
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien admissible as an H-2B nonimmigrant will be admitted for the period of the approved petition. Such alien will be admitted for an additional period of up to 10 days before the beginning of the approved period for the purpose of travel to the worksite, and up to 30 days (subject to the 3-year limitation) following expiration of the H-2B petition for the purpose of departure or to seek an extension based on a subsequent offer of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless authorized under 8 CFR 274a.12, the alien may not work except during the validity period of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on individual's stay — 3-year maximum and 60-day outside requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien's stay as an H-2B nonimmigrant is limited by the period stated in an approved petition. An individual who has held H-2A or H-2B status for a total of 3 years may not again be granted H-2B status until they remain outside the United States for an uninterrupted period of at least 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility under this rule will be determined during adjudication of admission, change of status, or extension of stay. Individuals eligible for a shorter period due to this rule will be admitted only for that shorter period. The 3-year/60-day limitation does not apply to H-2B aliens who did not reside continually in the U.S. whose employment was seasonal/intermittent or aggregate of 6 months or less per year, or to aliens who reside abroad and regularly commute to the U.S. for part-time employment. To qualify for exceptions, the petitioner must provide evidence documenting relevant absences (arrival/departure records, tax returns, records of employment abroad).

rubrics_metrics.name: Traded professional H-2B athletes rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a professional H-2B athlete who is traded from one organization to another, employment authorization for the player will automatically continue for 30 days after acquisition by the new organization, within which time the new organization is expected to file a new application or petition for H-2B classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new petition is not filed within 30 days, employment authorization ceases. If filed within 30 days, the athlete is deemed in valid H-2B status and employment continues until adjudication; if the new petition is denied, employment authorization ceases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution of beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries of H-2B petitions approved for named or unnamed beneficiaries who have not been admitted may be substituted only if the employer can demonstrate that the total number of beneficiaries will not exceed the number certified in the original temporary labor certification. Beneficiaries who were admitted to the U.S. may not be substituted without a new petition accompanied by a newly approved temporary labor certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To substitute beneficiaries previously approved for consular processing but not admitted with aliens outside the U.S., petitioner shall notify the consular office or port of entry by letter and copy of approval notice and submit evidence of qualifications. To substitute beneficiaries previously approved for consular processing but who are in the U.S., petitioner shall file an amended petition with fees, copy of original approval, explanation why substitution is necessary, evidence of qualifications and current status, and evidence that the number of beneficiaries will not exceed the certified number. The amended petition must retain a period of employment within the same half of the same fiscal year as the original petition; otherwise a new labor certification and petition are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Labor may investigate employers to enforce compliance with the conditions of a petition and Department of Labor-approved temporary labor certification to admit or otherwise provide status to an H-2B worker.

rubrics_metrics.name: FY2024 supplemental allocation eligibility and attestation requirements (Public Law 117-328; Public Law 118-15)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY2024 only, the Secretary authorized up to 64,716 additional H-2B visas (specified allocations) for returning workers (issued H-2B or granted H-2B status in FY2021–2023). Additional 20,000 visas authorized for nationals of specified countries (Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Haiti, Colombia, Ecuador, Costa Rica) not subject to returning-worker requirement. Petitioners seeking these allocations must comply with all statutory and regulatory H-2B requirements and submit, at filing, a DOL attestation evidencing irreparable harm, that workers requested were issued H-2B in FY2021–2023 (unless nationals counted under the 20,000 cap), compliance with additional recruitment obligations, documentary evidence upon request, and agreement to cooperate with DHS and DOL compliance reviews and audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must request nationals of listed countries in a separate H-2B petition and declare via attestation Form ETA-9142-B-CAA-8. Petitions requesting returning workers accompanied by an attestation indicating they request nationals of the listed countries will be rejected, denied, or approved only for beneficiaries from those countries. Petitioners may not change status to H-2B under this paragraph. Processing rules: USCIS will reject petitions received after numerical limits are reached or after Sept 16, 2024, or outside prescribed filing windows; USCIS may randomly select among petitions received on final receipt dates. This paragraph expires Oct 1, 2024. The attestation requirement is intended to be non-severable from the remainder of the paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing rules and numerical limitations for FY2024 supplemental allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will reject petitions filed under the FY2024 supplemental allocation rules that are received after the applicable numerical limitation has been reached or after September 16, 2024. For certain date ranges petitions will be rejected if received earlier than a specified number of days after the INA section 214(g) cap for the second half of FY2024 has been met. USCIS will make allocations in the order petitions are received, will project numbers necessary to achieve numerical limits, notify public of final receipt dates, and may randomly select among petitions received on final receipt dates if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the final receipt date is one of the first 5 business days that filings can be made, USCIS will randomly apply numbers among petitions received on any of those 5 business days. Petitions not randomly selected or received after final receipt dates will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: FY2025 supplemental allocation eligibility and attestation requirements (Public Law 118-47; Public Law 118-83)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY2025 only, the Secretary authorized up to 64,716 additional H-2B visas for returning workers (defined as persons issued H-2B or granted H-2B status in FY2022–2024) and up to 20,000 visas for nationals of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Haiti, Colombia, Ecuador, or Costa Rica (not subject to returning-worker requirement). Petitioners must comply with all statutory/regulatory H-2B requirements and submit a DOL attestation at filing demonstrating irreparable harm, prior issuance of H-2B status for requested workers (unless nationals counted toward 20,000 cap), compliance with recruitment requirements, documentary evidence upon request, and agreement to cooperate with DHS and DOL compliance reviews and audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners requesting nationals of the listed countries must request them in a separate petition and declare via attestation Form ETA-9142-B-CAA-9 as required under 20 CFR 655.68(a)(1). Petitions requesting returning workers that are accompanied by an attestation indicating nationals of the listed countries will be rejected, denied, or approved solely for beneficiaries from those countries. Petitioners may not change status to H-2B under this paragraph.
